full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 16.8.93 passed by the 2nd Additional Assistant Judge. Barisal in Title Suit No. 64 of 1992 rejecting the petitioner's application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for staying of all further proceedings of the suit till the disposal of Title Suit No. 213 of 1979 and Misc. Appeal No. 51 of 1988. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that opposite party Nos. 1-6 as plaintiffs instituted a suit in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Barisal being Title Suit No. 213 of 1979, praying for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 11.2.79 passed in Title Suit No. 225 of 1977 alleging inter alia that defendants obtained the said decree collusively and fraudulently by suppression of all legal processes and as such the said decree is liable to be set aside. 

 3. The petitioner as defendant contested the said suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the decree in Title Suit No. 225 of 1977 was obtained lawfully after meeting all legal formalities. It was further contended that there was no suppression of facts and no fraud was practiced upon the court and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Thereafter opposite party Nos. 1-6 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 64 of 1992 before the Second Court of Munsif at Barisal against 6 defendants (petitioner not being initially impleaded) alleging inter alia that the defendants are monthly tenant under the plaintiffs and they became habitual defaulters in payment of rent and ultimately refused to pay rent which necessitated the filing of the suit for their eviction. In this suit the present petitioner on his own volition got himself impleaded as a defendant in the suit on the ground that he is vitally interested in the suit property and as such his presence was necessary for proper and effective adjudication of the suit. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for staying all further proceedings of the suit till the disposal of Title Suit No. 213 of 1979 and Misc. Appeal No. 51 of 1988 of the Court of Second Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Barisal. 

 5. Opposite parties Nos. 1-6 resisted the aforesaid application by filing written objection denying all its material allegations contended inter alia that the property involved in the two suits is different. It was also contended that the matters in issue involved in the two suits are completely different and as such there was no application of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the present case. 

 7. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in view of the fact that a common question of title is involved in the 2 suits, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in not allowing the petitioner's prayer for staying all further proceedings of the suit till the disposal of Title Suit No. 213 of 1979 and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that in view of the fact that the parties in the 2 suits and the property involved in the 2 suits are different and issues involved in the 2 suits are substantially different, there was no scope for application for section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the present case and as such the learned Assistant Judge rightly passed the impugned order, which does not suffer from any illegality or legal infirmity that may justify interference by this court in revision. 

 9. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before me the impugned order as well as the plaints or Title Suit No. 213 of 1979 and Title Suit No 64 of 1992. It appears that the properties involved in the two suits are not the same and the parties thereto are also different. It appears that Title Suit No. 213 of 1979 was filed challenging the ex parte decree dated 11.2.79 passed in Title Suit No. 225 of 1977 on the ground of fraud and collusion whereas Title Suit No. 64 of 1992 has been filed for eviction of monthly tenants. The learned Assistant Judge on detailed discussion and proper consideration of the materials on record clearly found that since the issues involved in the two suits are substantially different and the subject matter of the 2 suits and the parties and property involved therein are also different, there was no scope for application of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the present case. 

 10. In support of his contention Mr. Abdul Quayum referred to me the case of Abdur Razzak Bhali and another Vs. Hajee Ashrafun Nessa and others, reported in 37 DLR, 271. In this case a Division Bench of this court held that to succeed in an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is necessary for the applicant to prove that all matters in issue in the two suits should be identical. 

 11. The expression "Matter in issue" has reference to the entire subject in controversy between the contending parties and the matters in issue in the two suits shall have to be identical. An applicant for stay of a suit under this section is bound to show that all matters in issue in the suit are directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit. An application is not entitled to the benefit of this section where some of the issues are identical in the two suits but others are different. It is also necessary for the applicant to show that the entire subject in controversy is the same in both the suits. The principle of law enunciated in the cited case supports the contention of Mr. Quayum. Consequently, it is found that sec-tion 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no application to the present case. 

 13. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the impugned order dated 16.8.93 passed by the 2nd Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Barisal in Title Suit No. 64 of 1992 is affirmed. The order of stay granted earlier by this court stands vacated. 

 15. In view of the fact that this is a very old suit it is necessary in the interest of justice that the suit be disposed of with utmost expediency. The learned Additional Assistant Judge is hereby directed to dispose of Title Suit No. 64 of 1992 within 6 months from the date of receipt of the lower court records.
